""Our brains don't like change, it stresses us out. We want to know what to expect. But COVID has taken away most of our certainty about the future. We can't plan ahead or look forward to much. And so there is this nagging stress that's been there for over a year now.""

""Being stressed causes our brain to make decisions using the Amygdala. This focuses on our immediate desires, without much thought for the future. It's the part that wants ice cream for dinner. And so we will naturally make poor decisions: bad food, late to bed, no exercise, etc""

""This also has a tendency to make us blame everything on external factors, and wait till things 'get better' before taking action to improve ourselves. Which is not useful. We thus need to actively filter out the Amygdala thinking, and think ahead.""

""But making improvements is hard, especially when you have to fight your brain to do it. So don't aim to make big changes. Just aim for 1% each day. That little bit more sleep, tiny bit less fat, extra few steps, etc. Then after 100 days you'll have reached your goal.""
